_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910002.text: Toronto have lost 13 straight to New York going back to January 2023, and their recurring problem has been letting games slip late. Scottie Barnes is back from his adductor strain, but Kawhi Leonard is still out with left knee swelling and Nate Bittle is also sidelined, while the defending-champion Knicks report a clean injury list. The news angle leans towards New York.

401910003.text: Portland coach Micah Nori returns to Minnesota, where he spent five seasons as Chris Finch's assistant, and admits it will be 'very, very weird' being back. The Timberwolves are without Anthony Edwards for at least two months after knee surgery, while Portland are still missing Ja Morant (hamstring) and this is the second game of a back-to-back between the teams. The angle leans slightly towards Portland keeping it close.

401910004.text: San Antonio are 12-2, on a 12-game winning streak and top of the power rankings, with Victor Wembanyama the reigning Player of the Week. Detroit arrive badly short-handed, without Jalen Duren, Ron Holland, Taurean Prince and Duncan Robinson, with Isaiah Joe doubtful, and they play at New Orleans the following night. The news angle leans clearly towards the Spurs.

401910006.text: Utah are depleted and on the first night of a back-to-back, without Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jaren Jackson Jr. (MCL), Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes. The Clippers are 4-8 and still waiting on Brandon Ingram, whose heel surgery also involved a partially torn Achilles, and Bradley Beal is out too, but they have won two straight behind Darius Garland. The angle leans towards the Clippers.

401910005.text: The Lakers have won eight straight but will be without Austin Reaves (heel bruise, third straight absence) and Walker Kessler (lower leg soreness). Luka Doncic is off the injury report despite rolling his ankle in Milwaukee, and this opens a stretch of four home games in seven days. The angle still leans to the Lakers, with less margin than usual.

401910007.text: Memphis are 7-0 on the road and have won four of five, but leading scorer Ty Jerome sat Monday with a sore hip and GG Jackson needs surgery on a broken foot. Cleveland have finished what Yahoo called a brutal early schedule with Donovan Mitchell scoring 39 against Chicago, but Evan Mobley will miss at least another 7-10 days with a sprained toe. Jerome's status is the swing; the angle is close to neutral with a slight lean to Memphis.

401910008.text: Indiana's injury list is long: Tyrese Haliburton's hamstring timetable is 'uncertain' per Rick Carlisle, and Ben Sheppard and Johnny Furphy are out long-term, with the front office reportedly shopping for upgrades. Houston opened a six-game road trip with a loss in Miami that Ime Udoka said 'wasted' a 32-point night from Fred VanVleet. The angle leans towards Houston.

401910009.text: A double homecoming: Tyler Herro returns to Miami for a tribute night, and Giannis Antetokounmpo faces the Bucks for the first time since the trade, calling it 'just another game'. Milwaukee are 1-13, their worst start in 52 years, while Miami have won five straight, though Bam Adebayo left Monday's game with hip tightness. Herro has extra motivation, but the overall angle leans towards Miami.

401910010.text: Orlando have won four straight, including their first win in Boston since 2022, and Jalen Suggs is back from an eight-game knee absence, though Paolo Banchero is still out. Philadelphia are 12-3 and top of the East, but Joel Embiid (plantar fascia) and LeBron James (back) are both on careful management plans. The angle leans slightly towards Orlando, with Embiid's availability the swing factor.

401910011.text: Nic Claxton faces Brooklyn, the team that traded him to Chicago, if his hamstring allows. The Bulls are 3-10, on a three-game skid and finishing a road trip without Caleb Wilson. Michael Porter Jr. is back from a personal absence, but executives expect Brooklyn to shop him and other veterans. The angle leans slightly towards Brooklyn.

401910012.text: Two struggling locker rooms: Washington have lost eight straight, fans are calling for Brian Keefe's job and The Athletic's Josh Robbins says it could be at risk, while Toronto have blown three leads in four days and Darko Rajakovic's late-game coaching is under fire. Toronto are at home but on the second night of a back-to-back, with a Kawhi Leonard knee update expected around now. The angle leans mildly towards Toronto.

401910013.text: New Orleans are in turmoil: Dejounte Murray has asked for a trade, coach Jamahl Mosley is under pressure after a run of 138-point defensive collapses, and Zion Williamson called the effort 'unacceptable'. They did, however, snap a six-game skid by routing Golden State on Monday, and Detroit arrive short-handed on the second night of a back-to-back. The angle leans towards the rested Pelicans despite the noise.

401910014.text: Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins return to Oklahoma City for the first time since leaving the title team for Atlanta, so expect an emotional night. The Thunder are without Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace, but Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored 40 and 37 in his last two. The angle leans towards the Thunder, with some extra fire from the returning Hawks.

401910016.text: Golden State are reeling: Stephen Curry is out with an oblique tear, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are in long-term rehab, Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away, and they had 'no juice' in a 21-point loss at New Orleans. Dallas have lost three straight, including a 37-point rout in Boston, and Kyrie Irving's knee is being managed. The angle leans towards Dallas.

401910015.text: Denver were booed after another 'inexplicable' home loss, to a Phoenix side on a back-to-back, leaving them 2-4 at home, and David Adelman said the '50-50 stuff just killed us'. Boston had their six-game streak snapped in Orlando, with Jayson Tatum playing through a bruised hand, but get a day of rest first. The angle leans slightly towards Boston, with a frustrated Denver looking for a response.

401910017.text: Utah have lost 12 straight, are without Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr., and play the second night of a back-to-back. The Lakers have won eight straight, and Walker Kessler, sent from Utah in a July sign-and-trade, could face his old team if his leg soreness clears. The angle leans clearly towards the Lakers.

401910018.text: Sacramento are 1-12, Doug Christie says 'this seat is hot always' when asked about his job, and Domantas Sabonis is reported to want out, with Charlotte and Toronto expected to pursue him. Phoenix won in Denver on Monday, though Jalen Green is the subject of trade talk involving Dejounte Murray. The angle leans towards Phoenix.
